educational_rationale.certification_relevance: Network+ N10-008 (Section 4.3 Network Security Appliances) & Security+ SY0-701 (Section 2.1 Threat Vectors & Discovery Tools)
educational_rationale.deep_dive: In a standard TCP 3-way handshake (SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK), a full connection is established. Nmap's SYN scan (-sS) sends a SYN packet; if the target replies with SYN-ACK (port open) or RST (port closed), the scanner immediately responds with RST rather than ACK. Because the handshake never completes, legacy applications frequently fail to log the attempt. SIEM/NIDS rules identify this pattern through bursts of incomplete half-open connections across sequential destination ports from an untrusted public IP.
